bull.b: Strong recurring-revenue growth combined with expanding large-enterprise adoption indicates durable platform demand. Larger customers and rising contract values can deepen switching costs, support cross-selling across security modules, and provide a solid base for continued subscription growth.

bull.t: Robust cash generation and balance sheet
bull.b: High operating and free cash flow give Zscaler meaningful capacity to fund product development, infrastructure, and go-to-market investment internally. Combined with improved capitalization and controlled leverage, this strengthens resilience and preserves flexibility for long-term strategic execution.

Momentum across AI security and Zero Trust Everywhere broadens the company beyond its original core offerings and increases the addressable use cases within existing accounts. This supports durable expansion through new modules, workload coverage, and higher-value platform adoption.

bear.b: The lower forward growth rate signals that Zscaler may be moving from exceptionally rapid expansion toward a more mature growth profile. If moderation persists, it could reduce operating leverage from incremental sales, temper expansion opportunities, and increase execution demands.

Despite improving EBITDA and operating margins, continued GAAP net losses indicate that the business has not yet converted its strong revenue and cash trajectory into consistent bottom-line profitability. This can constrain earnings quality and make sustainable returns harder to establish.

bear.t: Elevated infrastructure investment and lower cash conversion
bear.b: Higher infrastructure costs and sustained capital intensity may absorb more of the cash generated by the subscription model. A lower free cash flow margin reduces funds available for reinvestment, acquisitions, or balance-sheet strengthening and raises the execution burden on future growth.
